study.title: Correlation between the Effects of Acupuncture at Taichong (LR3) and Functional Brain Areas: A Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Study Using True versus Sham Acupuncture
study.study_design: Within-subject resting-state fMRI study comparing preacupuncture and postacupuncture brain function after sham and true acupuncture at LR3
study.blinding: Volunteers were not told the order of true or sham acupuncture; volunteers' eyes were masked with eyeshades and earplugs worn
study.population: Healthy subjects from universities and colleges in Guangzhou city, China
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) being between 21 and 28 years of age; right handedness; (2) having regular diet; minimal liquor, tobacco, tea, and coffee; normal sleeping patterns (before 12 a.m.); moderate size body mass index of 18.5–23.9 (Chinese); no history of nervous system disease; (3) having no pain (including dysmenorrhea) or insomnia within 1 month before the test; (4) having no metallic substances in the body, such as stents; (5) being fit for noise and hypothermia; no fear of confined spaces; (6) having not undergone acupuncture within 1 month before the test

conditions.timepoint_exact: 15 min after withdrawing the needle (sham acupuncture)

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: bilateral LR3 localized according to Name and location of Acupoints: Chinese National Standards GB/T12346
interventions.needle_type_exact: sham needle (blunt, nonpenetrating); tube: DONGBANG AcuPrime, Exeter, UK
interventions.penetration_exact: no penetration; tip touched skin without puncturing
interventions.manipulation_exact: The auxiliary part of the tube was applied to the skin, with a sham needle placed in the tube over the acupoint. The sham needle was then tapped to make its tip touch the skin without puncturing it and was maintained in place for 30 min.
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Subjects were asked to pass urine and stool prior to treatment. Volunteers' eyes were masked with eyeshades, and earplugs were simultaneously worn so their audiovisual system could not be stimulated.

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: bilateral LR3 localized according to Name and location of Acupoints: Chinese National Standards GB/T12346
interventions.needle_type_exact: Huatuo needles 0.30*(25 mm–45 mm), Suzhou Medical Supplies Co., Suzhou, China; tube needling technique
interventions.manipulation_exact: After removal of the tube, the needle was vertically punctured at 15 mm ± 2 mm. After developing needle sensation, twirling at an angle of 90–180° and frequency of 60–90 times/min and lifting and thrusting at a range of 0.3–0.5 cm and frequency of 60–90 times/min were conducted. After manipulating the needle for 1 min, the needle was held in place for 30 min. During the 30 min, physician repeated this manipulation for 1 min every 10 min.
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Subjects were asked to pass urine and stool prior to treatment. Volunteers' eyes were masked with eyeshades, and earplugs were simultaneously worn so their audiovisual system could not be stimulated.

extraction_notes.note: The tables label coordinates as 'Talairach (mm)' but the methods section states 'Rest1.8 software Viewer was employed to identify the precise anatomical position in the brain with statistical significance on the corresponding MNI coordinate.' It is ambiguous whether coordinates in tables are in Talairach or MNI space. Coordinates have been extracted as labeled in the table (Talairach) without conversion.

No formal deqi measurement instrument or scale was used. Needle sensation was described only as a prerequisite for manipulation ('after developing needle sensation') with no quantified deqi subscale scores reported.
No expectancy, credibility, or blinding success instrument was formally assessed or reported. Participants were simply not told the order of true versus sham acupuncture.
Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper.
No clinical or behavioral outcome measures were reported. The study focused exclusively on neuroimaging outcomes.

The study is described as within-subject (all 15 subjects received both sham and true acupuncture) with a fixed order: sham acupuncture first, then true acupuncture 30 minutes later. There is no randomization of order, which may introduce carryover effects.

The sham condition uses the same bilateral LR3 acupoint location as true acupuncture. The sham differs only in that the needle does not penetrate the skin. This means the 'control' is at the same anatomical site, not a different (non-acupoint) location.
The paper does not report voxel size or smoothing kernel FWHM explicitly. Smoothing is mentioned as 'space smoothing' without further detail for ALFF; for ReHo, 'space smoothing was not finished.'

No Brodmann area is listed in Table 2 for the SA versus PA contrast rows (Sublobar lentiform nucleus, Cerebellum posterior lobe declive from TA vs SA), and no Brodmann areas appear for several TA vs SA rows. This is preserved as reported.

The paper states preacupuncture scan was collected before sham acupuncture (subjects received sham first). It is unclear whether the 'preacupuncture' baseline scan serves as the baseline for both sham and true acupuncture conditions, or whether separate baselines were collected. The text implies a single baseline scan collected before sham acupuncture and used for all comparisons.

Table 2 row for 'Cerebellum posterior lobe, declive' under TA versus SA shows coordinates 33, -57, -15 with T=5.21. The X coordinate column appears to contain '33' but the Y and Z values '-57' and '-15' may be split across columns. Extracted as written in table.
The paper describes subjects as a within-subject sample (n=15) receiving both interventions. Arm sample sizes reflect the same 15 participants across conditions, not separate randomized groups.
